subject: A few things I noticed about Elite Auto Service's online presence
body:
Hi there,

I run a small studio that helps local auto shops capture more of the work that's already trying to reach them online. I came across Elite Auto Service and spent some time looking at how you show up on the web. Here's a quick, honest audit — no pitch, just what I found:

What's working
- Clear niche — ASE-certified with a Subaru specialty alongside domestic/foreign — and your hours are clearly published, which more shops get wrong than you'd think.

Where you're leaving money on the table
- No real way to book or request a quote online. There's a 'Request Service' button but no actual form — so it's effectively call-first. A lot of customers, especially younger ones, won't pick up the phone.
- Your reputation is invisible on your own site. You've got reviews on Google and Yelp, but none show up where someone is actually deciding between you and the next shop.
- No live chat for the quick "do you work on my Subaru?" questions that turn into booked work.
- The site is missing the behind-the-scenes Google markup (LocalBusiness/AutoRepair schema) that helps you surface for "auto repair near me."

None of this is urgent, and your specialization clearly stands out — but each of these is quietly costing you jobs that are already trying to reach you.

If you ever want, I'm happy to walk through how a couple of these could be fixed cheaply. Either way, figured the audit might be useful.

Best,
Leo Lebel
cheddar.lebel@gmail.com

subject: A few things I noticed about Primer Auto Body's online presence
body:
Hi there,

I run a small studio that helps local auto body shops capture more of the work that's already trying to reach them online. I came across Primer Auto Body and spent some time looking at how you show up on the web. Here's a quick, honest audit — no pitch, just what I found:

What's working
- Honestly, a strong setup — LocalBusiness schema with your hours, a contact form, AND a live chat widget already running (rare for a body shop). Plus an excellent reputation (Google ~4.9/31, Yelp 92, Birdeye 4.9). Nicely done.

Where you're leaving money on the table
- Your reviews aren't surfaced on the homepage — you link out to Google instead of showing the actual testimonials inline. Someone deciding between you and another shop never reads them. Pulling that text onto the page is a cheap, high-leverage win.
- You're closed weekends, so the chat and form are your only after-hours capture — worth making sure those leads get an instant response (or an after-hours auto-reply) so a Saturday accident inquiry doesn't cool off before Monday.

Honestly you're already ahead of nearly every shop out here, so this is fine-tuning, not fixing.

If you ever want, I'm happy to walk through how a couple of these could be tightened up cheaply. Either way, figured the audit might be useful.

Best,
Leo Lebel

subject: A few things I noticed about Sharpe Automotive's online presence
body:
Hi there,

I run a small studio that helps local auto shops capture more of the work that's already trying to reach them online. I came across Sharpe Automotive and spent some time looking at how you show up on the web. Here's a quick, honest audit — no pitch, just what I found:

What's working
- Honestly one of the best setups I've audited out here — full AutoRepair schema with your hours and an FAQ, online booking, and real customer testimonials with star ratings surfaced right on your own site. Well done.

Where you're leaving money on the table
- No live chat. You've got booking covered, but a lot of customers want to ask a quick question before committing — and those are exactly the visitors who turn into same-week work.
- You're weekday-only with no after-hours coverage beyond the booking form. A live answer or instant callback for evening/weekend calls would catch the leads that won't wait until Monday.

You're clearly ahead of the pack, so this is fine-tuning, not fixing — but each is a little leakage worth closing.

If you ever want, I'm happy to walk through how a couple of these could be tightened up cheaply. Either way, figured the audit might be useful.

subject: A few things I noticed about Rob's Automotive's online presence
body:
Hi Rob,

I run a small studio that helps local auto shops capture more of the work that's already trying to reach them online. I came across Rob's Automotive and spent some time looking at how you show up on the web. Here's a quick, honest audit — no pitch, just what I found:

What's working
- Good behind-the-scenes Google markup (AutoRepair schema with your location) and a contact/schedule form already in place. Solid foundation.

Where you're leaving money on the table
- Your testimonials section is there but empty — it's placeholder markup with no actual review text. So a visitor sees a 'reviews' heading and nothing under it, which reads worse than having none. Filling it with real customer quotes is a quick, high-impact fix.
- No live chat, and after-hours it's form-only with no weekend coverage.
- Your contact email runs through a Cox ISP mailbox (robs.sdcoxmail.com) — those are fragile (you lose it if you ever change providers) and can hurt deliverability. A branded address on your own domain is a cheap upgrade.

None of this is urgent — but each of these is quietly costing you jobs that are already trying to reach you.

If you ever want, I'm happy to walk through how a couple of these could be fixed cheaply. Either way, figured the audit might be useful.

subject: A few things I noticed about Superior Auto Body's online presence

Hi JR,

I run a small studio that helps local auto body shops capture more of the work that's already trying to reach them online. I came across Superior Auto Body and spent some time looking at how you show up on the web. Here's a quick, honest audit — no pitch, just what I found:

What's working

Where you're leaving money on the table
